author: Shohaku Okumura

relations.subject: Shohaku Okumura
relations.evidence: I formally became Uchiyama Rōshi's disciple... I stayed there until Uchiyama Rōshi retired in 1975. In February of that year, shortly before his retirement, I received Dharma transmission from him.

relations.subject: Shohaku Okumura
relations.evidence: So I went back to Komazawa University for another year, graduating in the spring of 1972, and began my practice at Antaiji soon after.

relations.subject: Shohaku Okumura
relations.evidence: In 1993 I moved to Minneapolis to teach at the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center... I taught as the interim head teacher there until 1996, and I remained a part-time teacher there for another year.

relations.subject: Shohaku Okumura
relations.evidence: in the summer of 1997 I moved to California and took a job as director of the Sōtō Zen Education Center (currently known as the Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center)

relations.subject: Chiko Corona
relations.evidence: Rev. Corona was at that time a disciple of Kenkō Yamashita Rōshi, who served as the abbot of Zenshuji and the Bishop of North America for many decades.

relations.subject: Chiko Corona
relations.evidence: (And after her teacher's death, she became my disciple.)

relations.subject: Shoryu Bradley
relations.evidence: another disciple of mine, Rev. Shoryu Bradley, worked several years on revising the series of articles into a single book.
